text: The LORD said to Moses:
"Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with a skin disease, everyone with a discharge, and everyone who is unclean through contact with a dead body.
Send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp, so that they do not defile their camp, where I dwell among them."
So the Israelites did this and sent them outside the camp. Just as the LORD had said to Moses, so the Israelites did.
The LORD said to Moses:
"Say to the Israelites: When a man or a woman commits any sin against another person, thereby breaking faith with the LORD, that person is guilty.
They must confess the sin they have committed. The guilty one shall make full restitution, adding a fifth of its value to it, and give it to the one who was wronged.

But if the wronged person has no close relative to receive the restitution, it belongs to the LORD and shall be given to the priest, along with the ram of atonement by which atonement is made for the guilty one.
Every contribution from all the holy gifts that the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to him.
Each person's holy gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest belongs to the priest."
The LORD said to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If a man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
if another man sleeps with her and it is hidden from her husband—she has defiled herself in secret, with no witness against her, and she was not caught in the act—

versions.text: if another man sleeps with her and it is hidden from her husband, and her impurity goes undetected because there is no witness against her and she was not caught in the act—
versions.explanation: The Hebrew states as fact that she has defiled herself (וְהִיא נִטְמָאָה) while remaining concealed (וְנִסְתְּרָה). The current wording turns this into 'her impurity goes undetected,' which blurs the two separate clauses and reads as a causal explanation ('because') not present in the Hebrew.

text: and if a spirit of jealousy comes over the husband and he suspects his wife, whether she has defiled herself or not—

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall also bring on her behalf an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour.* He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that brings sin to mind. [*footnote: About 3.5 pounds, or 1.6 kilograms.]

versions.text: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall also bring on her behalf an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that brings sin to mind.
versions.explanation: The measure 'a tenth of an ephah' is opaque to hearers; a brief footnote giving a modern equivalent would help without altering the text read aloud.

versions.text: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall also bring on her behalf an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour.* [*footnote: About 3.5 pounds, or 1.6 kilograms.]
versions.explanation: The second half of the Hebrew verse was dropped when the footnote was added: לֹא־יִצֹק עָלָיו שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא־יִתֵּן עָלָיו לְבֹנָה כִּי־מִנְחַת קְנָאֹת הוּא מִנְחַת זִכָּרוֹן מַזְכֶּרֶת עָוֺן — the prohibition of oil and frankincense and the description of the offering as a jealousy offering and a memorial offering bringing iniquity to mind. This material is essential and must be restored; the footnote on the measure can remain.

versions.text: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall also bring on her behalf an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that brings sin to mind.
versions.explanation: Two small refinements: לְבֹנָה is specifically frankincense, the resin used with grain offerings, rather than generic 'incense'; and the footnote giving a modern equivalent for 'a tenth of an ephah', which was added in an earlier round, appears to have been lost when the second half of the verse was restored. Restoring it keeps the measure intelligible to hearers without changing the spoken text.

text: The priest shall bring her forward and have her stand before the LORD.
Then the priest shall take holy water in a clay jar, and take some of the dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

After the priest has had the woman stand before the LORD, he shall loosen her hair and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, the grain offering for jealousy, while he himself holds the bitter water that brings a curse.

Then the priest shall put her under oath and say to her: 'If no man has slept with you and you have not gone astray into impurity while under your husband's authority, may you be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
But if you have gone astray while under your husband's authority and have defiled yourself by sleeping with a man other than your husband'—
here the priest shall put the woman under this oath of cursing—'may the LORD make you a curse and a byword among your people, making your womb miscarry and your belly swell.
May this water that brings a curse enter your body, so that your belly swells and your womb miscarries.' And the woman shall say, 'Amen. Amen.'
Then the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
He shall have the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and this water will enter her and cause bitter suffering.
The priest shall take the grain offering for jealousy from her hand, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
He shall take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar; after that, he shall have the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her and cause bitter suffering; her belly will swell and her womb will miscarry, and she will become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be cleared of guilt and will be able to bear children.
This, then, is the law for jealousy, when a wife goes astray and defiles herself while under her husband's authority,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he suspects his wife. The priest shall have her stand before the LORD and carry out this entire law for her.
The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman will bear the consequences of her sin."
